summary: Yoshiro Tamura (1921–1989) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo and Toyo University, later holding posts at Toyo University, the University of Tokyo (chair in Japanese Buddhism, 1972–1982), and Rissho University (~1979–1989).

Yoshitaka Iriya (1910–1998) worked in sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University under Takeshiro Kuraishi. He later held posts at Nagoya University (1955–1977), Kyoto University (professor, 1970–1974), and Kyoto Sangyo University (~1974–1981).

Yoshito S. Hakeda (1924–1983) specialized in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He held appointments at Columbia University, serving as Professor in 1966 and until 1983 as Associate Professor in East Asian Languages and Cultures and Religion.
Yoshitoyo Ohara is a scholar in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. His career includes attested affiliations with Kyoto University in 2006 and the Kyoto National Museum in 2016.

Yoshitsugu Sawai (b. 1951) is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at Tenri, Tohoku, and Harvard universities under Daniel H. H. Ingalls and John B. Carman. He was professor and dean at Tenri University (~1984–2017).

Yoshiyasu Yonezawa specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held posts as a researcher, lecturer, and teacher at Taisho University (attested 1998–2026) and as a visiting member at the Naritasan Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Yoshiyuki Kawazoe (b. 1947) works in computational materials science and Tibetology. He completed his D.Sc. at Tohoku University, where he served as an assistant (1975–1990) and professor at the Institute for Materials Research (1990–2012).

Yosho Nomura (1916–1997) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Rissho University (~1936–1939) and later served there as a professor (~1960–1986), as well as director of the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of Lotus Sutra (~1979–1987).

Youru Wang is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Temple University under Charles Wei-hsun Fu and Thomas J. Dean, and later served on the faculty at Rowan University (attested 2007–2018).
Youwei Kang (1858–1927) was a philosopher and sinologist. He founded Wanmu Caotang in 1890 and served in a post there from circa 1891 to 1898, where he taught Liang Qichao.

Yozo Taniyama (b. 1972) works in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tohoku University (~1991–1996) and later held posts there (~2012), as well as at Shitennoji University, St. Thomas University, Japan, and Sophia University.

Yu Daoquan (1901–1992) was a scholar in Tibetology and linguistics. He studied at Cheeloo University and under Jacques Bacot (~1934–1936), later serving as professor of Tibetan language and literature at Minzu University of China (~1953–1987).
Yu Yan Pang is a Buddhist studies scholar. Pang earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong, studying under supervisors Jing Yin and Cecilia Chan, and teacher Eric Kvan.

Yu-Chen Tsui is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology. Tsui completed master's studies at Columbia University under Chün-fang Yü, pursued doctoral studies supervised by Natasha Heller, and studied traditionally under Sheng Yen.

Yu-kwan Ng (b. 1946) specializes in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and sinology. He studied at CUHK and McMaster University under Yun-hua Jan, Graeme MacQueen, and Koichi Shinohara, holding posts at HKBU (1988) and National Central University (~1992–2001).

Yu-min Lee is a scholar in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. Lee studied under graduate supervisor John C. Huntington and held a post as professor at National Taiwan University (attested 2002).
Yuan Ren is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at McMaster University under the supervision of Phyllis Granoff (attested 1998).

Yuanxing Guo (1920–1982) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Gongga Rinpoche and Gangkar Rinpoche, and held posts at the Jinling Scriptural Press and the Institute of Chinese Buddhist Culture as a researcher.

Yuanying (1878–1953) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Tongzhi, Miaolian, and others. He was abbot of Jiedai, Tiantong, and Yongquan temples, founded Yuanming Lengyan School, and served as the first president of the Buddhist Association of China.

Yudru Tsomu is a scholar of Tibetology, history, and archaeology. She earned her PhD at Harvard University under the supervision of Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp, with advisory support from Mark Elliott, Janet Gyatso, and Philip A. Kuhn.
